column1: # PROME/registry/READS.tsv — the DECLARED boot-read manifest: which desk reads which surface, and HOW.
# Born 2026-08-31 ET (PROME, Will's word in-session 23:09 ET: "lets build READS").
# ⚠️ IT DOES NOT REPLACE THE PERIMETER HEURISTIC YET, AND MUST NOT BE QUOTED AS IF IT DOES. This is the
#   DECLARATION half only. `scripts/read_cap_check.py` still derives its perimeter by scanning charters and
#   will keep doing so until DAEDALUS's R7-stage-2 teaches it to read this file (see PROVENANCE below).
#   TWO DIFFERENT TOOLS, never call either one "the checker":
#     · `PROME/tools/reads_check.py`  — consumes THIS file today. Validates + measures what is DECLARED.
#     · `scripts/read_cap_check.py`   — the fleet read-cap instrument. Does NOT read this file yet.
#   ⇒ Ruling ④'s interim convention ("READ-CAP 0 within N discovered whole-read files; heuristic perimeter")
#     REMAINS LIVE for every read_cap_check verdict. It retires only when read_cap_check consumes this file.
# Canon for the byte budget stays AGENTS/DAEDALUS/BLUEPRINTS/READ_CAP.md; this file never restates a constant.
# ⚠️ DATE BASIS: filenames and `declared_on` are ET (PROME's clock). Will's rulings below are stamped
#   2026-09-01 UTC and were made the same evening, 2026-08-31 ~20:5x ET. Same night, two clocks.
# RULINGS IT ENCODES (Will, in-session 2026-09-01 in the WALTER window; relayed verbatim-in-substance
#   1. A cross-agent read belongs to the READER's perimeter. ONE PATH MAY APPEAR UNDER SEVERAL READERS —
#      that is CORRECT, never a duplicate to dedupe. The reader's boot mandates it; the reader pays the context.
#   2. Declare `reader` · `path` · `mode` · `source_boot_step`. (row_kind/declared_by/declared_on/notes are PROME's additions — see PROVENANCE below.)
#   3. A programmatic read COUNTS if its CONTENTS ENTER SESSION CONTEXT. If the tool only computes a
#   4. Until this file is consumed by the checker, every verdict travels with its perimeter:
#      "READ-CAP 0 within N discovered whole-read files; heuristic perimeter" — NEVER simply "clear".
# STATES / MODE VOCABULARY — `mode` is a claim about THE SESSION, not about the file:
#     whole         a session reads the entire file into context (a Read call, or a step that says so).
#     programmatic  a script reads it and its CONTENTS land in context (ruling 3's counting case).
#   NOT CAP-BEARING (declared so the read is VISIBLE, and so nobody later "discovers" it as a breach):
#     scoped        a named part only — a section, a header, a ToC-first drill (READ_CAP.md rule 8).
#     summary       a tool reads it and emits a BOUNDED output; the rows never enter context (ruling 3).
#   ATTESTATION rows carry mode `manifest-complete` and are NOT reads.
# ⛔ NO BYTE COLUMN, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. This file declares WHAT IS READ; the checker MEASURES at run
#    time. A stored byte figure is a stale mirror within hours — measured 2026-08-31: WALTER/CLAUDE.md step 1
#    carried IRAN_WAR.md at 20,288 B (live 21,438 B) and step 2 carried MEMORY.md at 46,327 B (live 13,956 B),
#    both true when written. `finding_plausible_stale_value_evades_review` · READ_CAP.md rule 13.
# TWO INDEPENDENT DEFECT AXES — do not collapse them. (a) CAP: is a cap-bearing read over budget?
#   The checker grades this. (b) PROTOCOL ACCURACY: does the boot step's VERB describe the operation
#   that actually runs? No instrument can grade this — the READER owns it, and declaring `mode`
#   honestly is where a mismatch becomes visible. A step that says "Read" over a bounded script call
#   is a defect even when the cap is satisfied (live instance: PROME:BOOT.md-3 over GATES.tsv, below).
# ⛔ AN UNATTESTED DESK IS *UNKNOWN*, NEVER CLEAN. A desk's manifest is complete only when THAT DESK's
#    ATTESTATION row says so. Rows without an attestation are a partial perimeter, and a check over a partial
#    perimeter must report UNKNOWN — reporting clean is the exact defect this file exists to retire
# ⛔ WHO MAY ATTEST — the rule that makes the line above enforceable rather than decorative:
#    AN `ATTESTATION` ROW IS VALID ONLY WHERE `declared_by` == `reader`. PROME may TRANSCRIBE a desk's
#    attestation (no desk can commit inside PROME/), but must then write the READER's name in `declared_by`
#    and cite the desk's own statement in `notes`. ⛔ `PROME(from-charter)` can NEVER attest: PROME reading
#    someone else's charter is INFERENCE, not attestation, and a desk's charter cannot know what its boot
#    session actually does. Without this rule the ⛔ above is defeated by a single row anyone can type —
#    found by a blind cold reader who built exactly that row (2026-08-31). Enforced in
#    PROME/tools/reads_check.py, and the selftest's negative control is a PROME-signed attestation for
#    another desk, which must NOT clear it.
# DECLARED OUT OF SCOPE by READ_CAP.md's own "what binds" table — recorded here so the next desk does not
# re-derive FLG's 8/28 flag: auto-loaded `CLAUDE.md` charters (context cost, not truncation) and
# `memory/auto/MEMORY.md` (a DIFFERENT 25,600 B auto-load cap — do not conflate the two constants).
# WRITE PATH: the READER owns its declaration, but no desk may commit inside PROME/ — so a desk declares by
#   packet to PROME/inbox/ (or at any live touch) and PROME registers the rows. `declared_by` records WHO
#   asserted each row, because `mode` is the field most likely to be filled in charitably by an author
# MAINTENANCE: append-only in spirit; retire a row by setting mode `RETIRED-<date>` with the reason in notes,
#   never by deletion — a read that was dropped is history a stranger needs.
# PROVENANCE: this file is the DECLARATION half of DAEDALUS's registered R7-stage-2 (~2026-09-14, named in
#   scripts/read_cap_check.py and READ_CAP.md §Enforcement, and promised to 30 desks in the 8/28 packets).
#   The CONSUMER half — teaching scripts/read_cap_check.py to read this instead of scanning charters —
